data.standardized_narrative: At the 2023 year-end the syndicate's opening gross claims reserves were GBP 596.9m. During 2023 there was a reported overall net surplus (release) in ultimate claims of GBP 23.0m driven by favourable claims development across most classes (notably casualty and motor back-year releases and a positive run-off on 2020 and prior years), partially offset by deterioration on certain 2020 wind events and continuing material exposures to major US hurricanes (Ida and Ian) and Covid-19 related business interruption reserves.

The short-tail account generated a GBP 6.6m gross back-year release.
The GBP 6.7m gross back-year release is largely driven by the auto account
A positive run-off of GBP 21.0m on the 2020 and prior years' reserves
Most litigation has developed favourably in the year
The 2020 wind events experienced deterioration in the year, resulting in the gross ultimate moving out from $102.7m to $111.0m
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) gross movement was not explicitly stated in a single gross 'movement in prior years' note. The report explicitly states a net surplus of GBP 23.0m (used here as the PYD and flagged as NET of reinsurance due to lack of a clear gross figure). A gross positive run-off of GBP 21.0m on 2020 and prior years is reported in the RITC note and several LOB-level gross back-year release figures are given (casualty GBP 7.0m, short-tail GBP 6.6m, auto GBP 6.7m). The claims development triangle is present (gross) but contains an aggregate '2013 and prior' column which was excluded per instructions. Some event impacts are reported in USD in the report and have been converted to GBP using the year-end rate reference in the report (approx GBP 1 = $1.27) for illustrative purposes; these converted amounts should be treated as approximate.
